test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 21 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following are edible polysaccharides?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch, alginates, pectins and chitosans**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Starch**: A widely consumed edible polysaccharide found in staple foods such as rice, wheat, maize, and potatoes. It serves as a primary energy source for humans.
 
• **Alginates**: Polysaccharides extracted from brown seaweeds, commonly used as a food additive for thickening, gelling, and stabilizing in products like ice cream and sauces.
 
• **Pectins**: Naturally occurring polysaccharides in fruits such as apples and citrus, often used in jams and jellies as a gelling agent.
 
• **Chitosans**: Derived from chitin, these are edible and are increasingly used in the food industry for their potential health benefits and preservation properties.
 
• These polysaccharides are considered safe for human consumption and widely used in the food industry for their functional properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polysaccharides**: Complex carbohydrates made up of long chains of monosaccharide units. They serve various functions such as energy storage (starch, glycogen) and structural components (cellulose, chitin).
 
• **Chitin**: A structural polysaccharide found in the exoskeletons of arthropods and fungal cell walls. While non-edible in its raw form, its derivative, chitosan, is edible and used in food processing.
 
• **Cellulose**: A structural polysaccharide found in plant cell walls. Though indigestible by humans, it serves as dietary fiber, aiding in digestion.
 
• **Food Additives**: Polysaccharides like alginates and pectins are often used as food additives due to their gelling, stabilizing, and thickening properties.
 
• **Nutritional Importance**: Edible polysaccharides like starch are vital for providing energy, whereas others like pectins and chitosans contribute to functional food properties, promoting health and wellness.
